title: Wolstenholme-FLT Connection Overview
content: Introduces the deep connection between Wolstenholme's theorem and Fermat's Last Theorem through Bernoulli numbers. Wolstenholme's theorem ($\binom{2p-1}{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^3}$) relates to $B_{p-1}$, while Kummer's criterion for FLT concerns $B_2, B_4, \ldots, B_{p-3}$. Bernoulli numbers are the common thread: both theories are facets of the arithmetic of cyclotomic fields $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$.
mathContext: The connection triangle: Wolstenholme's theorem concerns $B_{p-1} \pmod{p}$, Wolstenholme primes concern $B_{p-1} \pmod{p^2}$, and Kummer's criterion concerns $B_{2k} \pmod{p}$ for $1 \le k \le (p-3)/2$. All three are divisibility conditions on Bernoulli number numerators.

title: Bernoulli Number Numerator Extraction
content: Defines `bernoulliNum k` as the integer numerator of the $k$-th Bernoulli number from Mathlib's `bernoulli : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Q}`. This integer extraction is needed because divisibility conditions ($p \mid \text{num}(B_{2k})$) are central to the theory of regular primes. Uses `Rat.num` for the numerator of a rational number in lowest terms.
mathContext: The Bernoulli numbers $B_n \in \mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $\frac{t}{e^t - 1} = \sum_{n=0}^\infty B_n \frac{t^n}{n!}$. Key values: $B_0 = 1$, $B_1 = -1/2$, $B_2 = 1/6$, $B_4 = -1/30$, $B_6 = 1/42$. For odd $n \ge 3$: $B_n = 0$. The numerator $\text{num}(B_{2k})$ is the relevant quantity for regularity: $p$ divides $\text{num}(B_{2k})$ iff $v_p(B_{2k}) \ge 1$.

title: Regular/Irregular Primes and Complementarity
content: Defines `IsRegularPrime p` ($p \nmid \text{num}(B_{2k})$ for all $1 \le k \le (p-3)/2$) and `IsIrregularPrime p` (the negation). Also defines `irregularityIndex p` counting divisible Bernoulli numbers. Proves `regular_iff_not_irregular`: the two definitions are exactly complementary for primes $p \ge 3$. The first irregular primes are 37, 59, 67, 101, 103—discovered by Kummer himself. About 63% of primes are conjectured irregular (heuristic: $1 - e^{-1/2} \approx 0.394$ regular).
mathContext: $p$ is regular if $p \nmid \text{num}(B_{2k})$ for all $1 \le k \le (p-3)/2$. The irregularity index $i_p = |\{k : 1 \le k, 2k \le p-3, p \mid \text{num}(B_{2k})\}|$. Siegel's conjecture: $i_p$ follows a Poisson distribution with mean $\frac{1}{2}\log\log p$. The density of regular primes is $e^{-1/2} \approx 0.6065$.

title: Fermat's Last Theorem per Exponent
content: Defines `FLT n` as the statement that $x^n + y^n = z^n$ has no positive integer solutions. The formalization uses $\mathbb{Z}$ (integers) with positivity constraints rather than $\mathbb{N}$ to avoid subtlety with natural number subtraction. Notes that FLT is trivially true for $n \le 2$ in the usual sense (FLT is interesting for $n \ge 3$), and that $n = 2$ admits Pythagorean triples.
mathContext: $\text{FLT}(n)$: $\forall x, y, z \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}: x^n + y^n \ne z^n$. By Euler and Fermat, FLT holds for $n = 3, 4$. By Kummer (1850), it holds for regular primes. By Wiles-Taylor (1995), it holds for all $n \ge 3$.

title: Kummer's Criterion (Axiomatized)
content: Axiomatizes Kummer's 1850 criterion: FLT holds for all regular prime exponents. The proof (outlined in the docstring) uses the factorization $x^p + y^p = \prod_{k=0}^{p-1}(x + \zeta_p^k y)$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_p]$, where unique factorization holds when $p$ is regular (i.e., $p$ does not divide the class number $h_p$). Kummer showed that $p$ is regular iff $p \nmid h_p^-$ (the minus part of the class number), which by the Kummer-Herbrand connection equals the condition on Bernoulli numbers.
mathContext: Kummer's proof strategy: in $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_p]$, if $x^p + y^p = z^p$ with $p \nmid xyz$, the factors $x + \zeta_p^k y$ are pairwise coprime (up to units). If $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_p]$ is a UFD (regular $p$), each factor is a $p$-th power, leading to a descent argument. The class number $h_p$ measures the failure of unique factorization: $h_p = 1$ implies UFD, and $p \nmid h_p$ suffices.

title: Bernoulli-Harmonic and Wolstenholme-Bernoulli Connections
content: Two axioms capturing the deepest connections. First, `bernoulli_harmonic_connection` (Johnson 1975): $H_{p-1} \equiv -pB_{p-1} \pmod{p^2}$, linking the harmonic sum from Wolstenholme's theorem to Bernoulli numbers. Second, `wolstenholme_bernoulli_equiv` (McIntosh 1995): $p$ is a Wolstenholme prime ($\binom{2p-1}{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^4}$) iff $p^2 \mid \text{num}(B_{p-1})$. These show that 'extra' divisibility of $B_{p-1}$ by $p$ corresponds to 'extra' divisibility of the binomial coefficient.
mathContext: Johnson's formula: $H_{p-1} = \sum_{k=1}^{p-1} 1/k \equiv -pB_{p-1} \pmod{p^2}$. Since Wolstenholme gives $H_{p-1} \equiv 0 \pmod{p^2}$, we get $pB_{p-1} \equiv 0 \pmod{p^2}$, i.e., $p \mid B_{p-1}$. But this is already known from Von Staudt-Clausen. The Wolstenholme prime condition $p^2 \mid B_{p-1}$ is the genuinely stronger statement: only $p = 16843$ and $p = 2124679$ are known to satisfy it.

title: The Connection Triangle and Wiles' FLT
content: The culminating section proves `irregular_blocks_kummer` (contrapositive of Kummer's criterion: irregular primes cannot use Kummer's approach) and axiomatizes `flt_wiles` (FLT for all primes via Wiles' 1995 theorem). The `flt_regular_both_ways` theorem shows regular primes have FLT from two independent sources: Kummer (algebraic number theory, 1850) and Wiles (modularity of elliptic curves, 1995). The ASCII art 'connection triangle' in the comment summarizes the structural relationships.
mathContext: The triangle: $\text{Bernoulli } B_{2k} \to \text{Kummer criterion} \to \text{FLT}$ and $\text{Bernoulli } B_{p-1} \to \text{Wolstenholme}$. For irregular primes ($\exists k: p \mid B_{2k}$), Kummer's method fails but Wiles' theorem still gives FLT. The proof of `irregular_blocks_kummer` is a one-line application of `regular_iff_not_irregular`.
